title: Railroad summer job, first xylophone and teaching himself
summary: He earns about $38.50 on a railroad pick-up gang, buys a table-model xylophone and teaches himself from books and records because the town had no teachers.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Well I got $100.00 for that and then I worked on the railroad. I played with a couple -- I mean a couple of pals of mine, their father was on the railroaders, too --
Yeah.
So one of them was the head of the roundhouse there, and in the summertime a lot of the boys would get jobs with the railroad.
Doing what?
Oh, I was a pick-up gang. You know that we have to change the wheels underneath the boxcars --
OH? No kidding?
And the boxcars, they'd -- they'd repair the wood on the side --
Oh, yeah.
And they'd tear that off and put it back on and we'd have to pick that up and throw it in the or --
Yeah.
And bring the double wheels under, we didn't have -- had everything ground down.
Yeah.
And things like that.
So --
I think I saved -- I saved most of that. I think I had saved $38.50 or something and it was a -- enough to get a first one, which was a table-model.
Oh.
And I just monkeyed with it. I enjoyed just --
No lessons at all then, huh?
Not then. No I just monkeyed around with it. And later -- later --
So what would you --
-- later I found that'-- nobody taught, see there was no teachers in my town -- no music teachers, piano teacher. Nobody knew how to play that instrument.
Yeah.
There was nobody, I just got books and I listened to George Hamilton Green on records and --
Would you be using two mallets or -- what one?
Two mallets, yes.
Yeah.
And trying to get -- my mother would say well, you know, try and get it perfect, try and get it right, you know?
Yeah. She had that musical sense.
She said everytime you play it, try to do it better. Try do it --
Yeah, yeah.
So she kind of instilled in me the idea that --
Yeah.
-- she kind of perfected it -- good --
Yeah, I guess she was pleased to see that you --
Not -- they weren't -- nobody paid much mind to it.
Yeah, it's funny isn't it --
